newsitem.title: USA: Fed on look-out for faster inflation, Rivlin says.
newsitem.headline: Fed on look-out for faster inflation, Rivlin says.

text.p: The economy is "perking along" well at the moment but the Federal Reserve needs to be on the look-out for an acceleration in inflation that could undermine growth, Fed Vice Chair Alice Rivlin said Thursday.
"The economy is growing at a healthy clip, payrolls are up, unemployment is down," she told the National Community Reinvestment Coalition, "Incomes are beginning to rise."

"The challenge for the Federal Reserve in this respect is to try to keep this good news coming, especially to be vigilant against the threat of accelerating inflation which has so often derailed our economy in the past," she added.
Rivlin said that steady growth with low inflation and low interest rates would help community development.
"I can't promise that the Federal Reserve will deliver this," she said. "I can promise that we will do our best with monetary policy to keep the economy on track."

Rivlin said Congress and the Clinton administration could help as well. "An agreement between the president and the Congress to keep the federal budget deficit on its current and very gratifying downward track would help keep long-term interest rates ... down," She said. "So would an agreement to get the Social Security system onto a sounder foundation."
